FINDING_ID: IM_F001  
SEVERITY: 0.93  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.78  
DESCRIPTION: `DetectorHealthMonitor.record_round()` saves `new_diagnoses` into `self._diagnoses` before it appends remediation-outcome diagnoses and self-diagnosis results. Those later diagnoses are returned to the caller but not saved in monitor state, so `all_diagnoses`, `has_critical`, and any later history-based logic can miss CRITICAL immune failures.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Move `self._diagnoses.extend(...)` to the end of `record_round()`, or extend again after `_verify_remediation_outcomes()` and `self_diagnose()`. Add a test where `self_diagnose()` emits a CRITICAL diagnosis and `has_critical` becomes `True`.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F002  
SEVERITY: 0.91  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.83  
DESCRIPTION: The adaptive sensitivity loop is effectively broken. `effective_window()` ignores `self._sensitivity_decay`, and it never uses persistent pathology count to narrow the window. As a result, the “high false positive rate” self-adjustment changes a parameter with no runtime effect, and repeated pathologies do not speed detection as the comments claim.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Rework `effective_window()` so it uses both resolved-count and persistent-count inputs with the actual tunable parameters (`_sensitivity_decay`, `_sensitivity_growth`) in one consistent formula. Add tests showing that self-adjustments really change the trigger window.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F003  
SEVERITY: 0.89  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.76  
DESCRIPTION: `_verify_remediation_outcomes()` judges success using generic metric drift instead of checking whether the pathology actually stopped. For `kappa`, any increase clears the remediation even if it is still “stuck”; for `mu`, the code treats values up to 20% worse in absolute magnitude as “improved”. This can clear remediation state too early and block escalation to the next fix.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Make success criteria pathology-specific. Store a success predicate or threshold with each remediation step, and only clear the remediation when the underlying pathology is no longer true.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F004  
SEVERITY: 0.84  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.67  
DESCRIPTION: The `mu` pathology never updates its persistence state. In `record_round()`, the “mu increasing while findings stable/declining” branch emits a diagnosis but never increments `self._pathology_counts["mu"]`, even though later code reads that key for adaptive-window and resolution logic. This makes `mu` pathologies non-adaptive and prevents correct natural-resolution tracking.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Increment `self._pathology_counts["mu"]` when the diagnosis is emitted, and reset or resolve the same key when the condition clears. Keep the remediation key mapping explicit if `mu_distortion` is the external chain name.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F005  
SEVERITY: 0.86  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.72  
DESCRIPTION: `false_positive_rate` claims to be a recent-window metric, but its denominator counts all historical diagnoses in `self._diagnoses` with no round filter, while the numerator is windowed. Over time this pushes the rate downward even if recent false positives are bad, so the immune layer can stop self-correcting exactly when it should react.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Stamp every diagnosis with the round number, then compute both detections and natural resolutions over the same bounded window and the same diagnosis set.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F006  
SEVERITY: 0.82  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.70  
DESCRIPTION: The vocab-saturation detector ignores the shared immune config. `record_round()` hardcodes `0.04` and a 3-round window, while `DynamicManagementConfig` exposes `tau_vocab_growth` and `vocab_sustained_window` and documents a 5-round default. This creates split-brain behaviour: the health monitor can diagnose saturation on rules that do not match the manager’s actual stop logic.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Pass the relevant config into `DetectorHealthMonitor` and use `tau_vocab_growth` and `vocab_sustained_window` directly instead of local constants.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F007  
SEVERITY: 0.73  
FLAW_CLASS: 4  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.88  
DESCRIPTION: The “extended P-pass” safety gates are mostly declarative, not real iterative falsification. `_extended_p_pass_remediation()` and `_p_pass_self_adjustment()` loop several times, but they do not actually revise the candidate, rerun on changed inputs, or isolate the adversarial pass in a fresh context. That means the code reports multi-pass confidence without performing the protocol it claims to enforce.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Either downgrade these functions to honest single-pass heuristics, or implement true iteration: revise scope/parameters between passes, isolate the adversarial check, and stop only when a changed candidate survives a fresh pass.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

BOUNDARY NOTE: `apply_diagnosis()`, `_REMEDIATION_CHAINS`, and the full `process_round()` body were not shown. The detection code already mixes internal keys like `"kappa"`/`"kappa_stuck"` and `"mu"`/`"mu_distortion"`, so the next thing to inspect is the end-to-end key/metric mapping across those unseen interfaces.
